image_description: A cluttered room interior featuring multiple wooden bookcases. The central subject is a tall, dark wood bookcase filled with books and decorative objects. To the left is a lower shelving unit near a window, and to the right is a taller, lighter-colored cabinet or bookcase. A small white stool with a dark cushion sits in the foreground. The scene is lit by natural light from the left.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Rectangular furniture piece of considerable height, notably taller than wide.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The central bookcase is clearly rectangular and significantly taller than it is wide, matching the typical silhouette.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tall rectangular frame with horizontal divisions.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The structure consists of vertical sides and clear horizontal shelves creating distinct levels.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Bilateral symmetry with open front displaying books and objects.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: While the frame is roughly symmetrical, the contents (books/objects) are arranged asymmetrically, and the perspective angle breaks perfect bilateral symmetry. However, the structural design implies symmetry.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Multiple horizontal shelves spaced evenly from top to bottom.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: There are at least 5 visible shelves in the central unit, spaced relatively evenly.
Adjustability is an internal mechanical feature not visually verifiable from this distance/angle without seeing pin holes clearly.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Some models have glass doors on upper section.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: This specific model does not have glass doors; it is an open-shelf design. This is a valid variation, so the checkpoint is testable but the feature is absent.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Constructed from wood particleboard or metal with finished surface stained painted or laminated.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The texture and color indicate stained wood construction.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Front open displaying books and objects on each shelf.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The shelves are open and filled with books and various decorative items.
The wood has a visible finish/sheen, and there are decorative objects on the shelves.

artifact_observations.location: Spines of books on the central and left bookcases
artifact_observations.reasoning: The text on the book spines is illegible and appears as blurred, nonsensical patterns rather than distinct characters, a common AI artifact in detailed text rendering.

artifact_observations.location: Top right corner of the central bookcase and the object on top of it
artifact_observations.reasoning: The geometry of the items on the very top shelf and the corner of the bookcase itself appears slightly warped and fused, lacking crisp edges. The white object on top seems to melt into the background wall.

artifact_observations.location: The small white stool in the foreground
artifact_observations.reasoning: The legs of the stool have inconsistent thickness and perspective alignment; the front-left leg appears disproportionately thin and curved compared to the others.

artifact_observations.location: Books on the middle shelves of the central bookcase
artifact_observations.reasoning: The books lack individual definition; they appear as a fused mass of texture rather than distinct rectangular prisms, especially in the darker areas.

selected_experts.reason: To confirm the object is correctly classified as a bookcase and not a generic shelf or cabinet.
To verify the spatial relationship between the multiple bookcases and the wall, checking for background bleeding or floating elements.
To audit if individual books are distinct topological entities or if they are fused/melted together.
To assess the severity of the text gibberish and texture anomalies observed.

focus_areas: Legibility and structure of book spines (text artifacts)
Geometric integrity of book corners and edges (melting/fusion)
Structural plausibility of the stool legs
Boundary separation between books and shelves

Check if the 'structural_collapse' on the top right is a lighting issue or a genuine geometric failure.
